2. **The Model2Vec fused lift shrinks as n grows**: +31% at n=13, +11% at n=16, +1.7% at n=882. The pattern says the small-repo gains were noise, and at power, Model2Vec semantic on history is parity — consistent with the original "M2V is noise on history prose" probe. The question the Gemma runs will answer is whether the stronger embedder changes that, which is exactly what its clean separation on the 2026-06-08 probe predicted it might.

One honest caveat on "fix ollama": the brew formula was genuinely broken (ships no llama-server runner), and the cask app's binary wedges in `_dyld_start` when launched headlessly — it likely needs one interactive GUI launch from your login session to clear first-run verification. Rather than stay blocked, I stood up the spike's documented runner instead: node-llama-cpp serving the canonical `ggml-org` GGUF (the artifact alignment.md explicitly prefers over the Ollama blob) on `:11500` at ~17ms/embed. Embedding capability is fully working; the Ollama app itself could use one manual launch from you at some point.

  for questions settled negatively.
- Ranking: factLexicalScore unifies the lexical arm (term score + locus
  boost + closed-negative boost) for rankFacts and the fused ranker, so the
  two paths cannot drift. The boost applies only to already-matching facts
  and no existing fact carries the kind, so measured baselines are unchanged

## Changes

- **`closed-negative` kind** added to the closed set, top of inference priority. `closedNegativeCues` (ruled out / measured as noise / dead end / tried and failed / revisit only if / …) checked before gotcha cues — a dead end phrased as a trap is still a dead end. **Phase 2, item 1 is shipped** — PR #23 merged with all CI green. The `closed-negative` fact kind now exists end to end:

- **Kind + inference**: `closed-negative` in the closed set at top inference priority, with high-precision cues ("ruled out", "measured as noise", "dead end", "tried and failed", "revisit only if"…) checked before gotcha cues — a dead end phrased as a trap is still a dead end. A few extra gotcha cues landed alongside, chipping at the known 1-in-948 underfire.
- **Distill prompt**: a sixth kind with text-shape guidance (tried / why it failed / revisit-when, in one statement) and a new always-capture trigger for rejected designs, failed experiments, and measured non-levers — flagged as "the highest-value capture of all."
- **Ranking**: a new shared `factLexicalScore` (term score + locus boost + closed-negative boost) used by both `rankFacts` and the fused ranker so they can't drift. The +30 boost only applies to facts that already match, and since no existing fact carries the kind, every measured baseline stays bit-identical until new distills produce closed-negatives.

One deliberate non-action: I did *not* run `facts reclassify --force` on your live brain — force-mode would also overwrite agent-emitted kinds with inferred ones across all 948 facts, which is your call to make. A plain `reclassify` (fills only missing/invalid kinds) is safe whenever.

**Interim Gemma results** (entire-cli still running, ~2h): podcasts Gemma-fused hit **2.108 useful/1k vs 1.554 bm25 (+36%)** — a real lift. But entire-brain came in at 0.978, *below* its own Model2Vec-fused (1.219) and barely above bm25 — at n=13/16 these swing wildly, which is exactly why the n=882 entire-cli run is the one that decides. Full three-repo table when it completes.

fails (missing brain/repo is silence, only flag misuse errors), token-

Stopping here, as promised — I've hit a genuine decision point. Here's where things stand and the question.

## Shipped since "keep going" (all merged, CI green)

- **PR #23 — closed-negative fact kind** (Phase 2, item 1): the sixth kind with inference cues, distill-prompt hunting for settled-negative questions, and a ranking boost via a new shared `factLexicalScore`.
- **PR #24 — agent-harness hooks** (item 2): `hook pre-edit` (locus-anchored facts for the file being edited) and `hook post-failure` (gotcha/closed-negative matching on failure text), with a test-enforced harness-safety contract: silent empties, never fails, token-budgeted, warm-path only. Live smoke: pre-edit on `semantic.go` surfaces two real facts; everything else stays silent.
- **PR #25 — `brief --handoff`** (item 3): the session-resumption packet — last N distinct sessions with opening request and end-state decisions/validations, recent facts, and the sessions-since-distill blind-spot line. Live smoke on this repo's brain produces a genuinely readable trajectory (after fixing three data-quality issues the smoke test exposed: cross-branch session duplicates, tool-call JSON leaking into summaries, wrapper-injected requests).

## The Gemma verdict (recorded in the eval ledger)

| repo | n | substring | bm25 | fused-M2V | fused-Gemma |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| podcasts | 16 | 1.128 | 1.554 | 1.731 | **2.108** |
| entire-brain | 13 | 0.315 | 0.927 | 1.219 | 0.978 |
| entire-cli | **882** | 0.283 | 1.016 | 1.033 | **1.158** |

At real statistical power: Model2Vec-fused is **parity** with BM25 (the small-repo +31% was noise — the original "M2V is noise on history" probe was right), but **Gemma-fused is +14% with p=0.00075** (329W/248L on 577 informative pairs) — the same +14% the facts layer measured. The history semantic arm is now *validated, but only with the transformer embedder*.

## The question

That result creates a fork in priorities, and it's yours to call:

**Option A — productionize the Gemma-fused history arm now.** The measurement justifies it, but it's real work: query-time fusion over 267k records requires *persistent* history vectors (a one-time ~1.3h embed per big repo, then incremental on refresh), which means building the history vector store — naturally as vec0 under `brain_cgo`, looping back to Stage 1b — plus gating on a configured/reachable Gemma embedder, which today means a running local server.

**Option B — continue down Phase 2 in order**: item 4 (fact staleness/locus-drift signal) and item 5 (per-session incremental distill), which are pure agent-utility wins with no embedder-infrastructure dependency, and leave the history arm as a recorded, justified backlog item.

My lean is B — the Phase 2 items compound the delivery story you just started shipping, while A's value is capped until the in-process embedder lands anyway (a server dependency makes it opt-in-only either way). But A is the freshest validated win, and if the Librarian convergence is heating up, building the history vector store now front-loads shared-store work. Which way?

## Changes

- **`distill --session <id>`** — the bounded single-session path. Filtered sessions carry their cache entries through exactly like the `--branch` filter, so the next unfiltered run doesn't re-distill everything. `--session` + `--force` is rejected up front: force drops every distilled fact on the loaded branch but a session filter would re-derive only one session's — silent loss for the rest.
- **`hook session-end`** — deterministic refresh (agent=none, zero tokens) exports the just-ended session, then a distill bounded to it; proposals flow through the existing reconcile/review pipeline unchanged. Hook contract: empty stdout (summary to stderr), environment problems are silence. Unlike the warm-path hooks, this one may take minutes and spend tokens — the session is over, nobody is waiting. Re-fires are free via the incremental cache.

Session-filter semantics (only the named session costs agent calls; other sessions' cache entries survive even when their transcripts changed), the force-guard, and the existing hook-contract suite. Full suite green on both stacks.

content.text:
Found it — three compounding causes, one dominant. Here's the full diagnosis.

## Why the entire.io distill is crawling

**The dominant cause: the installed plugin binary is from Jun 7 — it predates the opencode-document stripping fix (PR #20, merged yesterday morning) — and entire.io is 75% opencode sessions.**

The numbers:
- **1,991 of 2,640 sessions (75%) are document-form transcripts** (opencode-style pretty-printed JSON), totaling **4.36 GB of the 5.63 GB corpus**, with files up to 52 MB.
- The Jun 7 binary's line-oriented preprocessor can't strip these — every line of an indented JSON document fails to parse individually — so they pass through **unstripped**: megabytes of tool output, diffs, and token accounting get chunked at 48 KB and fed to the agent. This is precisely the failure PR #20 fixed ("a 22.6 MB opencode session was 1.3% conversation text; the no-op strip cost ~75× the agent calls it should have").
- Unstripped, the document sessions alone are **~87,700 agent calls**. Stripped properly they'd be ~2–4 thousand.
- Each call spawns a fresh `claude --print` CLI process (Node boot + API round trip, no `--effort low` set either). Observed throughput: 881 sessions in 11h45m ≈ 48s/session — and the worst document sessions are mostly still ahead of the cursor. At this pace the remaining 1,759 sessions are **days**, not hours.

**Secondary findings:**
- **Concurrency isn't helping.** The binary has `--concurrency` (default 4), but the prefetch pool parallelizes chunks *within one session* — sessions are processed sequentially. I observed exactly one live `claude` child. For a corpus where stripped sessions are 1–2 chunks, cross-session parallelism is the lever that doesn't exist yet. That's a real architecture gap worth a backlog entry.
- **The Jun 7 binary also predates the pi-format routing fix** (`f02cd7f`), so any pi-style sessions distill to zero kept text, and it predates the closed-negative prompt — meaning the facts being produced are also lower-quality than what current main would extract. Some facts already written from raw-JSON chunks are likely junk-prone.

## Recommendation

Stop the run and restart on a current binary — the work isn't lost, and the broken sessions *should* be redone:

1. Kill the distill (pids 11801/11803).
2. Rebuild from main and replace `~/.local/share/entire/plugins/bin/entire-brain` (single static binary).
3. Restart: `entire brain distill --agent claude-code --model claude-haiku-4-5 --effort low`.

The incremental cache makes this surgical: fingerprints hash the *preprocessed* text, so the 649 JSONL sessions already distilled keep matching and are skipped, while document-form and pi sessions' fingerprints invalidate — exactly the ones that were being distilled as garbage — and they re-distill properly at 1–3 calls each instead of hundreds. Ballpark for the full corpus on the new binary: ~3–5k agent calls ≈ **5–10 hours** instead of days, with meaningfully better facts (current prompt, real conversation text).

Want me to do the kill/rebuild/restart? I didn't touch the running process — 11¾ hours of someone's run isn't mine to kill on a diagnosis question.

lookahead held ~0.2 work-sessions, so the producer never reached the next
session with real agent work before the consumer blocked.

structs) while a separate work-lookahead semaphore bounds the sessions
holding preprocessed chunk text — acquired before the transcript read,
released by the consumer when the session's chunks are fully consumed — so
memory stays bounded to ~concurrency sessions' chunks while skip streaks
flow through freely.

content.text:
The distill is now properly fast. PR #31 is merged (all CI green) and the live run is at 154/2640 after ~10 minutes. Here's what it took — three bottlenecks, each found by watching the live run, fixed, and verified live:

**1. Per-session call pool → cross-session pipeline.** The original prefetcher parallelized chunks *within* one session, but a stripped session is 1–2 chunks (the corpus median), so `--concurrency 8` ran ~1 call at a time. The fix is a producer/consumer pipeline sharing one call pool across sessions, with results applied strictly in chronological order so reconcile and fact application keep their serial semantics. One subtlety mattered: dispatch must happen from a *single* dispatcher in global consumption order — per-session dispatchers over a shared semaphore can hand a freed slot to a session the consumer isn't ready for, which deadlocks at small pool sizes.

**2. Lookahead counted sessions, not work.** First live restart still showed one call in flight: resuming past 881 cached sessions means ~95% skips, and a 4-session lookahead held ~0.2 work-sessions. Now the session buffer is deep (skips are near-free structs) while a separate work-lookahead semaphore bounds memory to ~`concurrency` sessions' chunk text.

**3. Serial preprocessing starved the pool.** Second restart: 2 of 8 slots used — parsing a multi-MB document costs seconds, and the single producer couldn't prep sessions as fast as the pool retired calls. Prep now runs in parallel workers (bounded by the same work semaphore), with delivery and dispatch still in order.

**Result, measured live:** the pool saturates at 8 and the run moves at ~15–23 sessions/min in the mixed region, versus **1.25/min** on the old binary — and that's with `--effort low` and `--max-chunk-bytes 131072` (fewer, bigger calls) also in effect. Honest ETA for the full 2,640: **roughly 2–4 hours**, since the uncached tail is all real work. Everything is race-clean and the full suite passes on both stacks; the existing semantics (consumption-bounded abort, lazy sequential `concurrency<=1`, flush cadence, cache rules) carry over with their tests.

One known serial element remains if you ever want more: reconcile calls run inline in the consumer (order-dependent by design), so fact-rich stretches still serialize on them. Worth touching only if the current run's tail proves slow.

The run is going in the background (`/tmp/entireio-distill3.log`); when it completes, the entire.io capstone validation (Phase 2 item 9) unblocks — the four-arm history eval on a fourth, TypeScript-domain repo. The interrupted entire-cli midtask measurement is also still queued; I'll pick both up as they're ready.

# Eval ledger

One row per retrieval-quality measurement that gated a decision. The task sets,
corpus snapshots, and metrics differ between rows — **numbers are comparable

## Closed negatives — do not re-litigate without new evidence

**Reopening discipline (worked example, 2026-06-10):** scan-cache v3 closed
"index request records" as measured ranking noise with no consumer. Phase 2's
handoff packet and midtask mining became new consumers — new evidence — so v4
reopened it *narrowly*: requests are extracted again for trajectory surfaces
while the original noise finding stands untouched (both rankers still exclude
them from general ranking). Closed negatives are reopened by new consumers or
new measurements, never by forgetting why they closed.

- **Query expansion:** early d≈0.47 was an n≈8 artifact; collapsed at n=121
  (d=0.10, p=0.26). Stays opt-in.
- **RRF fusion-weight tuning:** swept; all cells within noise. k0=60, equal
  weight stands.
- **Facts FTS5 BM25 as default:** parity, not better (1.43 vs 1.50). Opt-in.
- **History coverage-gate relaxation (3-of-N → 2):** added filler-word noise,
  regressed precision; BM25 is the fix, not gate tuning.
- **Scoped-floor (recall floor via backfill facts):** dead end; backfill facts
  don't help.

content.text:
**The powered midtask result is in, and it sharpens the story** (entire-cli v4 index, 1,522 tasks of which 632 are mined mid-session questions):

| arm | overall | midtask | code | concept | howto |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| substring | 0.272 | 0.260 | 0.373 | 0.173 | 0.231 |
| bm25 | 0.889 | **0.709** | 1.104 | 0.877 | 1.132 |
| fused (M2V) | 0.904 | **0.737** | 1.054 | 0.974 | 1.060 |

Two findings now have real statistical power:

1. **BM25's dominance is weakest exactly on the stratum agents actually query from.** Its lift over substring is 5.1× on opening concept queries but only 2.7× on midtask — narrow in-flight questions are lexically harder.
2. **Model2Vec-fused is parity overall (453W/425L, p=0.34) — consistent with the three-repo finding — but significantly positive on midtask (181W/144L, p=0.040).** Even the weak embedder helps where questions are narrow. That strengthens the case that the Gemma-fused arm's +14% overall understates its value for the hook-path/mid-task workload — which is exactly what item 8 existed to find out before shipping retrieval defaults for hooks.

Recorded in the eval ledger and pushed (`64affa6`). The Gemma midtask read joins the entire.io capstone batch.

Meanwhile the entire.io distill is at **721/2640 with 132 facts found** — sustaining ~15–19 sessions/min through real work (vs 1.25/min before the pipeline), tracking to finish in roughly 2 more hours. When it lands I'll run the capstone: four-arm history eval on entire.io, plus the Gemma midtask stratum read, and close out Phase 2 item 9's validation gate.
